errors.what: campaign refused: target had uncommitted changes (my fix)
errors.fix: committed the fix first, then ran the second campaign

doc_friction.issue: Step 1 says `redteam.py targets --probe 20` lists a file's suite time; `targets` prints a random 21-file sample, so grepping it for a chosen target printed nothing. Timing the suite directly with node --test was quicker.
Nothing says campaign refuses a dirty target, so a run that fixes a defect between campaigns must commit first; one line would save the retry.

deviations.why: Step 4b asks for a guard that runs without a red-team run; the defect class (a range check written for one unit branch only) has no sound text lint, and no other venture takes an mV coefficient (grep).
deviations.did: left the regression test in the venture suite (runs on every ventures/** PR) instead of a platform/ci lint

deviations.why: Step 0 has 11 open entries, all control-plane workflow edits already in owner-approval PRs (#14808, #14877, #15248, #15871, #14612...).
deviations.did: fixed none and seeded the full campaign

notes: Target chosen as never campaigned and safety-relevant (wash-sale-checker, the most-changed file, had 7 campaigns in 2 weeks). Seeded 22 mutants in 2 campaigns: 8/21 non-equivalent caught before, 21/21 after rerun. Real defect: mV/% coefficient plausibility gap allowed 12-module strings at 666 V on a 600 V inverter; patched with a failing-first test. Checks: run_venture_tests.py pv-string-sizer ok; node --test calc 27/27, page+usage pass.

real_defects.issue: Temperature-coefficient plausibility was checked only in % units and only for too-large values. The sample's -0.27 typed with 'mV per degree' selected (or -0.0027 %) was accepted silently and the tool allowed 12-module strings whose real cold Voc is 666 V on a 600 V inverter: an overvoltage answer. Fixed: both coefficients are checked as % of STC voltage whatever the unit, refused below 0.1 %/C or beyond 2 %/C in magnitude; failing-first test 'a coefficient too small to be real is refused'.
